STEP 1 - Scene: A small side dish of cooked leafy greens (looks like sautéed spinach or bok choy/greens) with thin shredded carrot and some pale stem pieces. Photographed from above, roughly top-down, on a white disposable plate placed on a glass-topped table.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White disposable plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side-plate size). Radius 10 cm, area = 3.14 x 10^2 = 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) cooked dark leafy greens (spinach/bok choy type), (b) shredded carrot, (c) pale green stem pieces. No visible oil pool or dressing beyond a slight sheen on the greens.

STEP 4 - Area: Greens ~14% of vessel (~44 cm^2); carrot ~2% (~6 cm^2); pale stems ~1% (~3 cm^2). Total food coverage ~17% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Greens 44 cm^2 x 2.5 cm = 110 ml; carrot 6 cm^2 x 1 cm = 6 ml; stems 3 cm^2 x 1 cm = 3 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Greens 110 ml x 0.15 = 17 g (cooked, loosely piled); carrot 6 ml x 0.6 = 4 g; stems 3 ml x 0.5 = 2 g. Total ~23 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked leafy greens ~25 kcal/100 g: 17 g → 4 kcal. Carrot ~35 kcal/100 g: 4 g → 1 kcal. Stems (bok choy-like) ~15 kcal/100 g: 2 g → 0.3 kcal. Total ~5 kcal, adding a small allowance for a little oil on the greens (~1 g x 884 ≈ 9 kcal) gives ~14 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest pile of a few handfuls of cooked greens with a little carrot should be roughly 20–30 g and well under 50 kcal. The estimate of ~23 g and ~14 kcal is plausible for the small visible amount.
